text: Removing an element during a for-each loop throws `ConcurrentModificationException` — except sometimes it does not. When?
choices: When the collection has fewer than three elements, since the check requires a full traversal.
When you remove the second-to-last element, because the iterator then reports no next element and the check never runs.
When the element removed is the first, since the iterator has not yet advanced.
Never — the exception is thrown deterministically on any structural modification.
explanation: Verified on a three-element list: removing "a" throws, removing "c" throws, and removing "b" silently succeeds and leaves `[a, c]`. That is worse than always throwing, because the code appears to work on the data you tested with. The check happens in `next()`, and after removing the second-to-last element `hasNext()` is already false. Use `removeIf`, or an explicit `Iterator` and its `remove`.
